newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei stages strong comeback, but trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei stages strong comeback, but trade thin.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key benchmark staged a strong comeback on Monday, gaining over 300 points in the course of the day after posting the biggest one-day drop this year on Friday, brokers said. But most market participants were still hesitant and trade was thin, they said.
The Nikkei 225 surged 327.01 points or 1.61 percent to 20,603.71. Its December futures settled 460 points up at 20,670.
"The U.S. markets' losses on Friday were smaller than expected which was a relief for Tokyo but investors still want to see how the European markets react," one broker said.

"It seems the Asian markets overreacted to the Fed chairman's comments," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd. "But a recovery to the pre-plunge level will be gradual and may take time."
Turnover dwindled to 237 million shares by the end of the Monday session, compared to 441 million shares on Friday as investors stepped back to see how other markets digest the Dow Industrials loss.
Buy-backs and bargain hunting hiked the number of advancing issues to 755, while the decliners totalled 305. There were 173 issues unchanged.
Haruo Nakaharu, Toyo Securities strategist said the market remained double-tiered, divided between promising, international, blue-chip issues and those that are not.

"Dealers especially were active today buying bellwether issues, but once they gained, profit-taking would push them back down again, limiting rises," he said. "Private investors are still dormant and domestic institutional were cautious, unless they come to life, the Nikkei will be range bound." Brokers added that unless demand in smaller issues picks up or the blue-chip demand broadens to encompass more stocks, upward momentum may be limited.
In other indices, the broader TOPIX was 15.76 points or 1.04 percent higher at 1,532.77. The Nikkei 300 rose 3.15 points or 1.10 percent to 290.14.
The second sector index gained 0.67 point or 0.03 percent to 1,927.42. Turnover was 5.7 million shares against 9.97 million on Friday.

Women's clothing retailer Suzutan Co slipped 19 yen to 447 after sources close to Japan's securities watchdog said it had begun a probe into alleged improper insider trading by the firm's president. It was the seventh largest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.

Ricoh Co Ltd was the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange in a volume of 5.22 million. It added 40 yen to 1,330 yen as market participants moved to buy back bellwether shares they sold off on Friday.
NTT shares jumped 38,000 yen to 883,000 yen as investors continued to buy on the telephone giant's restructuring plans.
Sector-wise, mining, warehouses, shipbuilding, textile and precision instruments led the gainers. Insurance and land transport were the main retreaters. --Masako Iijima, Tokyo
